div.head: Ps Cn for 26
div.ab: Episcopi, abbates et barones mei non calumniabuntur pro uenatione, si non regales feras occiderint; et si regales, restabunt rei regi pro libito suo, sine certa emendatione.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 624 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: My bishops, abbots and barons shall not be accused for hunting, if they have not killed royal beasts; and if [they kill] royal ones, they shall remain liable to the king at his pleasure, without fixed compensation.

note.seg: Heinrich II. fordert auch geistliche Forstfrevler vor sein Gericht; Bened. G. Henr. I 105; Diceto I 402. 410; Assisa for. c. 9. Schon das Concil von Lillebonne bestimmt 1080 für die Normandie: si presbiter forisfecerit de forestis, nullam emendationem inde habebit episcopus

Henry II summons clerical forest offenders, too, before his court; Bened., G. Henr. I 105; Diceto I 402. 410; Assisa for. c. 9. Already the Council of Lillebonne in 1080 lays down for Normandy: si presbiter forisfecerit de forestis, nullam emendationem inde habebit episcopus

jagende Mönche verspottet noch das 14. Jh. (Günther Engl. Leben 14. Jh. 467), aber die Charta de for. 11 nennt 1217 unter dem Adel, dem sie ein bis zwei Stück Wildpret beim Durchreisen des Forstes erlaubt, nicht Abt oder Prior. Doch genoss dies Privileg jeder Lord of parliament; Coke IV Inst. 309

The 14th century still mocks hunting monks (Günther, Engl. Leben 14. Jh. 467), but the Charta de for. 11 of 1217 does not name abbot or prior among the nobility whom it allows one or two head of game when travelling through the forest. Yet every Lord of parliament enjoyed this privilege; Coke IV Inst. 309

quicumque episcopus uel baro transierit per forestam, liceat capere 2 bestias (Charta for. 11), probably including harts, but not any number of head and not at all times. The author falsifies in the interest of the barons; cf. 30 note l

hohe Barone posuit in misericordia pro uenatione Heinrich II. 1175; Bened. G. Henr. I 94. Statt des technischen misericordia sagt auch Assisa Henr. II, 16: finem et redemptionem ad uoluntatem [regis]

Henry II in 1175 posuit in misericordia pro uenatione high barons; Bened., G. Henr. I 94. Instead of the technical misericordia, Assisa Henr. II, 16 also says: finem et redemptionem ad uoluntatem [regis]

Der Hochadel und Kronvassall darf also auch innerhalb des Königsforstes jagen, nur den Hirsch ausgenommen, doch natürlich nur, was zu ergänzen ist, im eigenen Walde, nicht im fremden oder krondomanialen. Der Abt von Battle erhält das Privileg, durchreisend 2 feras zu erlegen; Davis Reg. Agnorm. *263. — Über die Behandlung geistlicher Forstfrevler im 13. Jh. s. Turner p. lxxxvij

The high nobility and tenant-in-chief may therefore hunt within the royal forest too, the stag alone excepted, but of course only (this must be supplied) in his own wood, not in another’s or in the Crown demesne. The abbot of Battle receives the privilege of killing 2 feras when passing through; Davis Reg. Agnorm. *263. — On the treatment of clerical forest offenders in the 13th century see Turner p. lxxxvij
